challenges.name: bm25-parameters-quiz
challenges.title: What do k1 and b do?
challenges.description: Predict how BM25 treats repeated words and long documents before you implement it.

questions.question: Two help articles both mention "refund" twice. Article A has 60 words, article B has 600 words; the corpus average is 150 words. With the default b = 0.75, how does BM25 score the term "refund" for them?
questions.explanation: b controls length normalisation. The denominator of the term-frequency part grows with |D| / avgdl, so the same two occurrences are worth more in the short article (60 / 150 = 0.4) than in the long one (600 / 150 = 4): in a short text, two mentions say much more about what it is about. With b = 0 both would score the same; with b = 1 the length effect is at its strongest.

options.text: Higher for A: the same occurrences count for more in a shorter document.
Higher for B: longer documents are more likely to be thorough.
It depends on k1 only; b affects the IDF.

questions.question: Which statements about BM25 are true? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: The term-frequency part f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * ...) saturates: it grows quickly for the first occurrences and flattens towards k1 + 1, so the tenth occurrence adds far less than the second - keyword stuffing stops paying off. With k1 = 0 the part is f / f = 1 for any f > 0, so a term only counts by presence. With the +1 inside the logarithm, IDF stays positive even for a term found in every document, and a query term found in no document never contributes because f = 0 everywhere. Doubling a document's length lowers, not raises, its score for the same occurrences.

options.text: The tenth occurrence of a term adds less to the score than the second.
With k1 = 0, a term contributes only by being present, however often it appears.
A query term that appears in every document gets a negative IDF.
Doubling a document's length (same occurrences) doubles its score.

challenges.name: bm25-ranker
challenges.title: Write bm25_rank(docs, query, k)
challenges.description: Replace the raw TF-IDF ranking with Okapi BM25: IDF(t) = ln((N - n(t) + 0.5) / (n(t) + 0.5) + 1), and a term-frequency part f * (k1 + 1) / (f + k1 * (1 - b + b * |D| / avgdl)) that saturates and normalises for length. Each distinct query term counts once. Return the top k documents with a score > 0 as [[id, score], ...], best first, scores rounded to 4 decimals at the end; equal scores keep the corpus order. Honour k1 and b when given (defaults 1.5 and 0.75), and return [] for an empty corpus or query.
